context: Interactive data visualization triptych showing three coordinated views of the same network graph: force-directed layout, radial edge bundling, and chord diagram, with linked hover highlighting across all panels.
first_impression: A cohesive, deliberately designed three-panel network explorer with an intentional Tol bright palette and satisfying cross-panel highlight linking, let down slightly by a sparse force-directed layout and a dense, hard-to-parse central hairball in the bundling panel.
what_works: The Paul Tol bright palette is a deliberate, accessible choice used consistently across all three views — far above schemeCategory10 defaults. The linked hover dispatch system elegantly fades-to-dim across all three panels simultaneously, making the interaction the clear centerpiece.
what_doesnt: The force-directed panel's node clusters float in the upper-left of a large white panel with unconvincing use of space — the layout doesn't fill its 386×494 container confidently. The radial edge bundling's central mass of gray curves is visually impenetrable at rest; 8px node labels are borderline too small and several bottom-arc labels appear rotated and cramped.
